algorithm: Check if n < 2: return False (since primes are positive integers greater than 1).
Check for trivial factors (divisors other than 1 and n) up to sqrt(n). If found, return False.
For n <= 2^64: use deterministic Miller-Rabin tests with bases known to have no counterexamples in the range.
For n > 2^64: perform a strong BPSW primality test (probabilistic but with no known counterexamples).
Reject floats and non-integer inputs as per the contract.
constraints: n must be an integer in the range [-20, 10000] (per contract).
Floats are rejected as input (must be integers).
The algorithm uses deterministic tests for n <= 2^64 and probabilistic tests for n > 2^64.
edge_cases: n = 2^64 + 1: large number requiring strong BPSW test
n = 1e23: float input rejected (must be integer)
inputs: An integer n in the range [-20, 10000] (per contract), but note that negative numbers are not prime and floats are rejected.
output: A plain Python bool (True if n is prime, False otherwise).
purpose: Determine if an integer n is prime (True) or composite (False).
